title: IESCO Bill Calculator 2026 (Latest Tariff) | Wattlyst
meta: Estimate your IESCO bill from units with the 2026 NEPRA slabs, fixed charge, QTA, GST and the latest NEPRA FPA. Why winter bills run high.
author: ali-ahmad

sections.h2: What is the IESCO per unit rate in 2026?
p: IESCO does not set its own rate. It supplies Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Attock, Chakwal and Jhelum, with some feeders into Azad Kashmir, and bills the uniform A-1 domestic tariff that NEPRA determined and the Government notified for 2026. An unprotected home pays the rate of the slab its monthly units reach on every unit: 300 units are all billed at Rs 33.10. The lowest slab is the cheapest and the open-ended top slab is the dearest.

Protected and lifeline consumers have their own low rates, worked out slab by slab. The table below prints the rate for each slab from the tariff file, and the worked examples show a protected month, a winter heater month and a summer AC month.

sections.h2: Why is the winter IESCO bill as high as the summer one?
p: Islamabad and Rawalpindi have real winters, and when gas pressure drops many homes switch to electric heating. A fan heater draws about 2,000 W and a storage geyser about 3,000 W, so a few hours a day of each adds hundreds of units to the month. That is how a home that was protected in autumn lands at 450 units and a bill of Rs 24,358 in January.

Summer in the capital region is milder than south Punjab, but an inverter AC still adds a few hundred units. The AC units calculator estimates the units for your tonnage and hours; this page then turns those units into the IESCO bill.

sections.h2: IESCO bill check: estimate here, confirm on the IESCO site
p: This IESCO bill estimate works from the units you type. The official bill, with the reference number, due date, arrears and the exact FPA, is on the IESCO website, which links the duplicate bill page on the PITC portal; enter the reference number from the top of any earlier bill there. Use this calculator to understand what each printed line should be, to plan next month, or to check a high bill against the slab it should fall in.

If the reading dates on the bill cover more than a month, the units may have been pushed into a higher slab by the long cycle; the bill audit tool checks that for you. Every bill also carries an FPA line; see what the FPA line on your bill means. A home on a time-of-use meter can check the peak hours for IESCO.

l.t: what the FPA line on your bill means

faq.q: How do I get an IESCO bill estimate from my units?
faq.a: Enter the units and the sanctioned load from the bill, tick protected only if the bill says so, and replace the pre-filled FPA with the one on your bill under advanced settings. For 300 units the estimate is Rs 14,186, FPA included.

faq.q: What is the IESCO per unit rate for a home?
faq.a: The uniform NEPRA domestic slab rate for the slab the month reaches: Rs 33.10 per unit for an unprotected home using 300 units. The table above lists the rate for every slab; protected and lifeline consumers pay less.

faq.q: What is the IESCO tariff for 2026?
faq.a: The uniform A-1 domestic tariff notified as SRO 279(I)/2026: lifeline slabs up to 100 units, protected slabs up to 200 units, unprotected slabs of 100 units each up to 700 and an open-ended top slab. Connections of 5 kW and above are billed on ToU rates.

faq.q: How do I check my IESCO bill online?
faq.a: The IESCO website links a duplicate bill page on the PITC portal; enter the reference number printed at the top of an earlier bill to see the current bill and its due date. This calculator estimates the bill from units; it does not fetch your account.

The federal capital Islamabad and the districts of Rawalpindi, Attock, Chakwal and Jhelum, with some feeders serving Azad Kashmir. If your bill carries another company's name, use that company's calculator; the slab rates and the FPA are the same, but the official bill and reference number come from that company.

faq.q: Does an electric heater make an IESCO home unprotected?
faq.a: It can. Protection needs all of the last 6 bills at or under 200 units. A fan heater of about 2,000 W run a few hours a day adds well over a hundred units a month, which is enough to cross the limit.

faq.q: Why does my IESCO bill differ from this estimate?
faq.a: The estimate uses the pre-filled FPA unless you enter your bill's, and it cannot see arrears, late payment surcharge, meter rent or a long reading cycle. Copy the FPA rate from the bill, and if the reading dates cover more than a month, run the bill audit tool.

faq.q: Why is my real bill higher than this estimate when it is over Rs 25,000?
faq.a: Usually because of advance income tax, which this estimate leaves out: a domestic consumer not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List pays 7.5% on a monthly bill of Rs 25,000 or more. Who pays the income tax line is explained with the electricity bill calculator.

l.t: Who pays the income tax line

key_facts: IESCO, the Islamabad Electric Supply Company, bills the uniform NEPRA A-1 domestic tariff for 2026 across Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Attock, Chakwal and Jhelum, so 300 units cost the same in Rawalpindi as in Lahore apart from the monthly FPA line.
An unprotected IESCO consumer using 300 units pays Rs 33.10 on every unit, which is Rs 9,930 of energy charge before the fixed charge, FC surcharge, QTA and GST.
A heater month of 450 units in an Islamabad winter costs about Rs 24,358 unprotected, while the same home stays at about Rs 3,372 in a protected month of 180 units.

Protection on IESCO needs every one of the last 6 bills at or under 200 units on a connection below 5 kW; one winter month over the limit moves every later bill to unprotected rates until the run is rebuilt.
GST at 18% is charged on the energy charge, fixed charge and surcharges together and adds Rs 2,164 to a 300 unit IESCO bill; the surcharge and GST defaults are secondary-source figures that change.

The bill jumps at 700 units: up to there every unit is billed at Rs 41.85, but one unit more moves all of them to the top slab rate of Rs 47.20, which adds Rs 4,481 to the bill of an unprotected 1 kW home.

Income tax is not in this estimate: under section 235 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001, a home not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List pays advance income tax of 7.5% on a monthly bill of Rs 25,000 or more; consumers on the list pay none.
mistakes: Searching for a separate IESCO tariff. IESCO bills the uniform NEPRA domestic slabs; the FPA that moves month to month is one national figure for every DISCO.
Planning the winter on the autumn bill. A heater and a geyser can double the units in January, and one month over 200 units ends protected status for the next 6 bills.
Reading the reference number wrong on the duplicate bill page. Type the digits only, without the spaces or dashes some bills print between groups.
Dividing the bill total by units to find the IESCO per unit rate. Fixed charge, surcharges and GST are inside the total; the slab rate is the energy line divided by units.

fields.name: units
fields.label: Units on the IESCO bill
fields.hint: Units (kWh) for the month, from the bill or from this and last month's meter readings. Winter heater months and summer AC months both push this up.

fields.name: sanctioned_kw
fields.label: Sanctioned load
fields.hint: The kW printed in the connection details of the IESCO bill. It sets the fixed charge. A connection of 5 kW or more is billed on peak and off-peak (ToU) rates instead: use the ToU bill calculator.

fields.name: protected
fields.label: Protected consumer
fields.hint: Tick only if the bill prints the protected category; one heater month over the limit removes it.

fields.name: lifeline
fields.label: Lifeline consumer (up to one hundred units)
fields.hint: Only for very small consumers whose bill shows the lifeline category.

fields.name: period
fields.label: Billing quarter for QTA
fields.hint: The quarterly tariff adjustment depends on the quarter the bill falls in.

fields.name: fc_surcharge_per_unit
fields.label: FC surcharge
fields.hint: Financing cost surcharge per unit, from the bill. Secondary-source default.
fields.placeholder: Blank = Rs 3.23 per unit (none on lifeline or protected)

fields.name: fpa_per_unit
fields.label: FPA
fields.hint: Pre-filled with the latest NEPRA-verified fuel adjustment, the one for July 2026 charged on September 2026 bills. October 2026 bills carry Rs 1.11 per unit for August 2026, reported in the news; this page keeps the latest NEPRA-verified rate until that decision is published. Replace it with the FPA rate printed on your bill (negative is a credit). Protected homes pay it too; lifeline bills carry none.

fields.name: fpa_units
fields.label: Units in the FPA month
fields.hint: NEPRA charges the FPA on the units of the month it adjusts (the FPA month, usually two months before this bill), not on this month's units. Copy that month's units from the units history on your bill. Blank = this month's units.

fields.name: gst_pct
fields.label: GST
fields.hint: Sales tax applied to the bill subtotal.

legal.t: This is an estimate, not an official bill. Your DISCO's bill and NEPRA's tariff notifications are the official figures. Do not use this result as evidence before a court, NEPRA, the Wafaqi Mohtasib or any other forum. To dispute a bill, complain to your DISCO first, using the complaint number printed on your bill, then file a NEPRA complaint or a Wafaqi Mohtasib complaint.

examples.title: 450 units, winter month with a fan heater and geyser
examples.text: The heater month breaks the protected run, so all 450 units are billed at Rs 38.95 = Rs 17,528, fixed charge Rs 500, FC surcharge Rs 1,454, QTA Rs 234, FPA Rs 926, GST Rs 3,716. Estimated IESCO bill Rs 24,358.

examples.title: 300 units, unprotected, no AC or heater
examples.text: 300 × Rs 33.10 = Rs 9,930, fixed charge Rs 350, FC surcharge Rs 969, QTA Rs 156, FPA Rs 617, GST Rs 2,164. Estimated IESCO bill Rs 14,186.

examples.title: 550 units, summer with an inverter AC, 2 kW connection, FPA from the bill
examples.text: 550 × Rs 40.22 = Rs 22,121, fixed charge Rs 1,350 for 2 kW, FC surcharge Rs 1,777, QTA Rs 286, FPA Rs 825, GST Rs 4,745. Estimated IESCO bill Rs 31,104 including the FPA entered.

content.answer: An IESCO home in Islamabad or Rawalpindi using 300 units in a month as an unprotected consumer on a 1 kW connection pays about Rs 14,186: Rs 9,930 energy charge at Rs 33.10 per unit, plus fixed charge, FC surcharge, QTA, the July 2026 FPA and GST. IESCO bill = units × slab rate + fixed charge + surcharges, then GST on the subtotal.

formula.text: Bill = units × slab rate + fixed Rs/kW × sanctioned kW + (FC + QTA + FPA) × units, then + GST
lines: slab rate = rate of the band the month's units reach (unprotected) or slab-wise (protected)
fixed = Rs per kW of the band reached × sanctioned kW
FC, QTA, FPA = per-unit surcharges printed on the IESCO bill
